items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: Ed Thigpen, yes, and of course Kenny Clarke, the late Kenny Clarke, the late Leo Wright who played with Dizzy, and there were some great musicians who got jobs in the studio.

ctx.x: Ed Thigpen, yes, and of course Kenny Clarke, the late Kenny Clarke, the late Leo Wright who played with Dizzy, and there were some great musicians who got jobs in the studio. Herb Geller, an alto saxophonist, white American, he went over there and so did Sal Nistico.

items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he was on my first recording session, Here’s Comes Frank Foster, done in 1954.

ctx.x: Can I just ask another question? Kenny Clarke, you played with Kenny Clarke. You played with Boo, Art Blakey. You played with Elvin. But what was playing with Kenny Clarke like?

It was great. I loved it. I played with Kenny Clarke with one of my -- he was on my first recording session, Here’s Comes Frank Foster, done in 1954. I played with him on a couple of other subsequent recordings. I’m ashamed not to remember, but it was a good experience. But no experience will stand out like that of playing with Elvin. That was --
